versions.how_we_got_here:
The Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil above $100 for much of 2026, raising fuel, food and transport costs across Europe. In France that has revived the anger of the 2018 Yellow Vest movement.

On 7 November more than 140,000 people marched in Paris, Lyon and other cities. Police used tear gas and made arrests, and Yellow Vest groups defied a ban on their Paris rally.

players.name: French government
players.wants: Keep order and avoid a repeat of 2018-style riots.

players.name: Protesters and Yellow Vest groups
players.wants: Relief from high living costs and a change of direction.

players.name: Opposition candidates, such as Jean-Luc Mélenchon
players.wants: To turn anger into votes ahead of the presidential race.

versions.stakes: Political stability in the eurozone's second-largest economy. Prolonged unrest would hit consumer spending, French bonds and the government's room to act.
versions.current_state: As of 8 November: large, partly violent protests on 7 November; the interior minister says police are ready for rioters and looters. The size of any follow-up wave is unclear.
versions.watch_next:
- Whether protests recur next weekend and grow.
- Any government concessions on fuel or prices.
- How the presidential campaign picks up the anger.

timeline.event: Yellow Vest protests begin over fuel prices.
Brent tops $100 as the Iran war closes Hormuz.
140,000+ rally across France; tear gas in Paris and Lyon.
